BLOCKER: AC-3 is not designed: open question on whether object/cache/queue expose counters means per-store SLO dashboards/alerts cannot be shown to exist; no adapter instrumentation files are in scope.
AC-4 is not designed: quota enforcement and per-store degradation switches reference `go/edpsvc/internal/limits` but no affected file, config schema, or test defines quotas/switch behavior per store.
DB access for benchmark and EXPLAIN capture has no least-privilege/read-only role or RLS enforcement; “tenant-safe” invariant lacks a boundary control and risks admin/RLS-bypass DSNs.
MAJOR: AC-1 lacks baseline artifact definition: no storage location, versioning, environment fingerprint, variance tolerance, or retention for recorded baselines, so repeatability is not verifiable.
AC-1 failure case “missing DSN -> skipped scenarios” can produce a green run without per-store coverage; it should fail closed or record explicit skipped-store evidence.
AC-2 prod enforcement is underspecified: no environment detection and no hard production cap preventing `sample_rate=1.0`; sampling-only policy can be bypassed by config.
AC-2 `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes statements; no read-only transaction, statement allowlist, statement timeout, or rollback guard is defined.
AC-2 redaction of parameters/tenant data is declared but has no mechanism or test evidence; captured plans can leak literals/tenant data.
AC-3 validation is weak: Python config tests do not prove Prometheus rule semantics, alert lead time, or Grafana dashboard/schema validity; scrape/eval intervals remain open.
AC-4 “bounded” degradation is not quantified: no max duration, auto-expiry, quota-denied metric, or alert-routing handoff is defined.
SLO thresholds are not tied to measured baselines; open deployment overrides and aspirational values risk alert noise or missed regressions.
MINOR: Benchmark reconstruction metadata is incomplete: concurrency, dataset seed/size, host class, and run duration should be recorded with baselines.
Mixing SLO policy and runtime quota/degradation policy in `config/edp-slo.json` blurs ownership and rollback boundaries.
Captured EXPLAIN artifacts need explicit retention and access-control policy beyond “redacted”.
Quota enforcement observability lacks clear denied/allowed counters and bounded store labels.
NIT: `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py` is acceptable as tooling, but its prod guardrails should be documented alongside ops runbooks.
Single evidence doc `docs/EDP-22-BENCHMARKS-SLOS.md` should index baseline artifacts, rule files, dashboards, and per-store proof.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally sound on bounded labels, fail-closed regression, and default-off rollout, but AC-3 and AC-4 are not yet demonstrable.
Top risks: missing per-store SLO/counter coverage, undefined quota/degradation implementation evidence, and insufficient DB privilege/RLS and EXPLAIN redaction controls.
AC-1/AC-2 need stronger repeatability, environment, sampling, and read-only execution contracts before Gate 1.5.

`failure_taxonomy` omits `BENCH_STORE_SKIPPED` and `CONFIG_INVALID`, which appear in the failure matrix.
Scope/component lists omit `go/edpsvc/internal/explain` and `cmd/explain` despite being declared files and AC-2 entrypoints.
EXPLAIN artifact retention, access-control, and redaction details are asserted but not concretely specified or tested.
Synthetic `t-bench` tenant provisioning/cleanup is not defined, so RLS-scoped non-empty-read assertions may be non-deterministic.

Top risks: SLO thresholds not grounded in measured baselines, generated artifacts not validated, and degradation expiry/renewal semantics undefined.

BLOCKER: AC-4 quota enforcement is entirely absent: no `internal/limits/quota.go`, no call sites, and nothing emits `edp_quota_allowed_total`/`edp_quota_denials_total` yet the alert `ProductForgeQuotaDenied` and dashboard panel 5 query them — AC-4 cannot be satisfied and the alert can never fire.

AC-1 baseline evidence declared in the contract (`engineering/benchmarks/BI-PF-1314/README.md`, `db/local/baseline.json`, `db/local/metrics.prom`) is not in the diff, and `config/edp-slo.json` contains thresholds with no baseline ID reference — violates the "SLO thresholds are set from measured baselines, not invented targets" invariant.

Store metrics and degradation are dead code: `observe.Recorder` and `degrade.Check` have no store-adapter call sites in the diff, so AC-3/AC-4 ("demonstrated per store") and the runtime contract `store adapter -> degrade.Check -> fixed degraded error + observe metrics` are unproven.
MAJOR: `bench.Compare` ignores `MaxError` when a result has an error (`if r.Err != "" { violation; continue }`), and `MaxError==0` is treated as "unset" in the group override — `max_errors` config is effectively dead.
`edp_store_latency_ms` is emitted as a last-value gauge via `Set`, not the histogram the observability contract requires; p95/p99 store SLOs are therefore impossible from this metric.
`edp_bench_errors_total` is written as 0/1 per run from a file sink — non-monotonic value under a `_total` counter name, so any `rate()`/`increase()` over it is wrong.
`observe.Recorder.Request` passes the caller-supplied `outcome` string straight into a label with no allowlist; only `store` is bounded, so cardinality/leak risk remains.
`ProductForgeBenchmarkLatencyRegression` hardcodes `> 500` while `config/edp-slo.json` sets db to 250 — rules are hand-written, not generated/validated for drift against config as Slice 4 requires.
`db_explain_capture.py` validates but never enforces `--per-minute` or any concurrency cap; the design invariant requires both probability and per-minute/concurrency budgets.

No audit record (actor, statement label, sample decision, artifact path) is produced for EXPLAIN runs, and `--out` writes to an arbitrary path with no retention/access-control enforcement — violates the audit/security contract.

Production cap is client-asserted: `--env` defaults to `PF_ENV`/`dev`, so a mis-set env allows `--sample-rate 0.1` against production; no separate explicit prod-enable switch as the non-goal requires.
`expires_at` renewal tracking/"renewals are alerted and bounded" is not implemented; `Config` is loaded once with no reload path, so operators cannot force-expire without a redeploy.

`config/edp-slo.schema.json` and `config/edp-degradation.schema.json` (contract + CTL-CONFIG-SCHEMA) are missing; `validate_edp_slo.py` only asserts alert names/panel presence, which is a tautological no-drift check.

`[OUT_OF_SCOPE]` `scripts/dev/review_ledger.py` now returns `[]` when no delta entries exist, silently disabling the `FULL_REVIEW_MISSING` gate for delta items (review-tooling behavior change, CL-002 territory).
MINOR: `config/edp-degradation.json` has `"stores": {}` — no per-store switch demonstrated and the test loop is vacuous.

Bench scenario semantics silently changed (`kind 'note'→'semantic'`, `acl_scope 'team'→'project'`) with no rationale; this alters what is measured and is close to the out-of-scope "data-model changes of the stores" line.
Freshness alert `time() - edp_bench_last_run_unixtime > 86400` never fires when the metric is absent; needs an `absent()` companion for a never-run suite.
`cmd/bench` default `-baseline config/edp-slo.json` is cwd-relative while the documented invocation runs from `go/edpsvc`; only the doc example's explicit path saves it.
No `Load` validation test for `expires_at` exceeding `max_duration_seconds` or for `max_errors` handling; `slo_test` only exercises `Compare` happy paths.
EXPLAIN redaction is regex-only (quoted literals, 4+ digit numbers); UUIDs/emails/timestamps outside quotes and `tenant_id` column values in plan output are not covered.

NIT: `psycopg` is imported lazily with no pinned dependency/requirements entry for the tooling path.
`PrometheusSink` overwrites the sink file per run; there is no rotation or run-id comment header for traceability.
`validate_edp_slo.py` hardcodes `REQUIRED_GROUPS` including `artifact` while bench `scenarios()` groups are not cross-checked against config.
SUMMARY: Direction is right: bounded labels, fail-closed degradation errors, sampled EXPLAIN guard, and offline asset validation are solid foundations.

Not mergeable as-is: quota enforcement is missing entirely (AC-4), baseline evidence artifacts and baseline-ID linkage are absent (AC-1), and neither metrics nor degradation is wired into store adapters, so AC-3/AC-4 are only unit-tested, not demonstrated.

Observability contract mismatches (gauge latency, non-monotonic `_total`, hand-written rule thresholds) will let SLO drift go undetected; fix before the EDP-24 evidence gate relies on these baselines.

BLOCKER: `go/edpsvc/internal/observe/metrics.go`: after replacing `edp_store_latency_ms` with `ObserveHistogram`, the local `ms` and its negative clamp are left unused; Go rejects unused locals, so `go test ./...` cannot build.
`go/edpsvc/main.go` `cacheHandle`: `tenant` is required but never namespaces the key; `/admin/cache` GET/PUT/DELETE can read or overwrite another tenant’s cached bytes, bypassing tenant isolation.
MAJOR: `main.go`: any error from `degrade.NewPolicy` — including invalid `config/edp-degradation.json` — is swallowed and replaced by an empty policy instead of startup refusal, violating `CONFIG_INVALID` and fail-closed behavior.
`degrade/policy.go`: the new renewal counter is only returned by unused `RenewalCount`; no metric/alert/bound is emitted, so degradation can be renewed indefinitely without detection.
`cache/memory.go` + `main.go`: the store has no capacity/eviction bound and the handler always calls `Set` with `ttl=0`; the admin cache can grow without limit and never expires.
`bench/slo.go`: for `MaxError > 0`, any scenario with `Err != ""` is accepted, so a positive `max_errors` disables all error violations rather than bounding counts.

`scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`: `--state`/`--audit` are optional, the rate check is non-atomic, and there is no concurrency cap; the required per-minute/concurrency/audit guarantees remain bypassable.
`main.go` object store: quota is only reached via `/admin/object-store/conform` with `tenant=""`, so `Quota` is skipped for object store and real object operations remain unguarded.
MINOR: `db_explain_capture.py`: `rate_ok` consumes a slot even when sampling later skips the run, causing false `REFUSE` under normal sampled-out traffic.
`degrade/policy.go`: `Policy.Check` takes a global mutex and `os.Stat`s the config on every store operation, serializing hot-path calls and adding filesystem I/O.
`storeguard/guard.go`: `Do` checks only `g == nil`, not `g.Degrade`; a zero-value `Guard` panics instead of failing safe.
`validate_edp_slo.py`: sibling `import gen_edp_slo` inside `problems()` depends on `sys.path`; imported-module/pytest execution can fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
`validate_edp_slo.py`: alert presence is checked by substring, not exact rule/alert name, so a summary or comment can satisfy the check.
NIT: `db_explain_capture.py`: state/audit file opens are not context-managed; state writes are not atomic.
`audit` records are append-only with no rotation/fsync/retention enforcement in the tool.
`gen_edp_slo.py` hardcodes non-benchmark alerts while `validate_edp_slo.py` separately hardcodes required names; generation and validation can drift in the non-generated portion.
SUMMARY: The delta fixes several prior gaps (generated SLO rules, store guard wiring, histogram metrics, baseline references) but introduces a build blocker and a tenant-isolation bug in the new admin cache.
Remaining enterprise risks: silent degradation-config fallback, unbounded cache, incomplete `max_errors` semantics, and EXPLAIN controls that remain optional/non-atomic.
AC-4 per-store quota is not demonstrated for object store; the only object guard path skips quota with an empty tenant.
Blockers must be fixed before merge; majors should be fixed or explicitly accepted with runbook controls.

MAJOR: `main.go` degradation startup guard: only refuses when `PF_EDP_DEGRADATION_CONFIG` is set; an invalid/malformed default `config/edp-degradation.json` still falls back to an empty policy, silently disabling AC-4 fail-closed `CONFIG_INVALID` behavior.

`degrade/policy.go`: hardcoded `p.renewals[store] > 3` makes `Check` return `ErrDegradedExpired` for every operation once a store has accumulated renewals, with no reset/alert in the hunk; healthy or removed rules cannot recover without process restart.

`bench/harness.go` + `bench/slo.go`: `Measure` breaks on the first error, so `Errors` is effectively 0/1; any `max_errors >= 2` can never be exceeded, silently disabling the error SLO bound the delta intends to enforce.

`cache/memory.go`: eviction triggers on `len >= 10000` by deleting a random live entry, including when `Set` is only updating an existing key; capacity is hardcoded and untracked by an eviction metric, so one tenant's writes can churn/evict other tenants without visibility.
MINOR: `cache/memory.go` / `main.go`: tenant namespacing is implemented only at the handler (`tenant + ":" + key`); the cache store API remains tenant-unaware, so any future direct caller can bypass isolation.
`db_explain_capture.py`: a sampled-in request refused by `rate_ok` is returned without an audit record, so the audit log does not capture the sample/refusal decision.
`main.go` object conform now requires `tenant`; no delta update to callers/runbook, so existing operator scripts invoking the admin endpoint without `tenant` will break.
NIT: `cache/memory.go`: random map-range eviction is non-deterministic and ignores TTL/expiry, which can make cache/bench behavior less repeatable.
`db_explain_capture.py`: the new state/audit requirement applies only when `sample_rate > 0`; the skip path still calls `audit(None)` if audit is absent.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves the prior build/unused-local and handler tenant-prefix issues, but several fixes are incomplete at the boundaries.

Top risks: default degradation config can still be silently swallowed; renewal cap can permanently fail-closed without recovery; benchmark error counts cannot enforce `max_errors>1`; cache eviction can cause cross-tenant churn without metrics.

MAJOR: **AC-4 / `go/edpsvc/internal/degrade/policy.go`**: the delta *deletes* the renewal bound entirely instead of bounding it with reset+alert; design invariant "renewals are alerted and bounded" and failure-matrix `degradation expired/renewed too often -> fail closed + alert (DEGRADED_EXPIRED)` are now unenforced, and `p.renewals` becomes write-only dead state.

MINOR: **AC-1 / `go/edpsvc/internal/bench/harness.go`**: with `continue`, latency samples exclude failed ops while `Ops` counts attempts, so p50/p95/p99 are computed on a smaller denominator than reported; a store failing all ops now runs to completion with an empty sample set, risking a passing baseline/SLO from zero samples (no delta test covers this path).

**`go/edpsvc/internal/bench/harness.go`**: errors after the first are only counted, never summarised (no error class/aggregate), making SLO regression triage harder than necessary.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves the earlier startup-guard and `Measure` fail-fast defects, and adds the missing rate-refusal audit; no new blockers.
Top risks: the degradation renewal invariant was removed rather than bounded (AC-4 regression), and the EXPLAIN audit now stores raw SQL instead of a statement label (AC-2 redaction drift).
Secondary: benchmark latency/SLO denominators diverge from attempt counts (AC-1 repeatability), and fail-closed startup lacks an observable `CONFIG_INVALID` signal.

**AC-4 / `degrade/policy.go`**: `delete(p.renewals, store)` on any `!ok || !nr.Enabled` makes the "bounded" invariant defeatable — flipping the switch off/on silently resets renewals to 0, so the bound is not enforceable and the reset is unaudited/unalerted contrary to "renewals are alerted and bounded".

**AC-4 / `degrade/policy.go`**: the delta adds the bound but emits no metric/alert for renewal count or threshold crossings; failure-matrix `DEGRADED_EXPIRED -> fail closed + alert` is only half met, and `ErrDegradedExpired` conflates true-expiry with renewal-limit so operators cannot distinguish causes.

**AC-2 / `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`**: only the audit *key* is renamed to `statement_label`; the value is still `a.query` (raw statement text), so the prior redaction concern is relabelled not remediated — disposition "ACTIONED" is not evidenced by this hunk.
MINOR: **`scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`**: renaming `query` -> `statement_label` is an unversioned schema change to persisted audit records; existing/retained audit logs and any consumer parsing `query` break, and runbook/docs in the delta are not updated.

**AC-4 / `degrade/policy.go`**: renewal threshold `3` is a hardcoded magic number decoupled from `config/edp-degradation.json` / `max_duration`, so it cannot be tuned per environment without a code change.
**AC-4 tests**: the delta adds renewal-reset and `>3` fail-closed semantics without corresponding changes to `policy_test.go`, so the new behavior is not fail-ably pinned.
NIT: **`test-framework/tests/test_db_explain_capture.py`**: assertion still only checks `"captured" in text`; it does not assert the `statement_label` key is present or that raw text is absent, so the rename is untested.
**`degrade/policy.go`**: `> 3` (fourth renewal) vs `>= 3` boundary is undocumented and off-by-one ambiguous for reviewers/ops.
SUMMARY: Prior MAJOR (renewal bound) and audit-label findings are only partially addressed: the bound was re-added but is unbounded-lifetime, resettable, and unalerted; the audit change is a key rename, not redaction.
Top risks: indefinite store lockout during legitimate extended incidents, silent bound bypass via switch toggle, and unversioned audit schema drift with raw statement text still persisted.
Verdict: not ready — AC-4 bounding is not robust/observable and AC-2 redaction is not demonstrably fixed by this delta.

BLOCKER: AC-4 / `degrade/policy.go`: window pruning runs only inside the "expiry extended" branch of `reload()`, while `Check` compares raw `len(p.renewals[store])`; once renewals exceed `RenewalLimit` and no further config edit occurs, the store stays fail-closed indefinitely (no time-based recovery), so the advertised time-windowed bound does not actually apply at read time.

Recovery from that state exists only via process restart or switch off/on (which wipes the ledger), i.e. the fail-closed state has no bounded expiry — violates the availability guardrail and the "renewals are bounded" invariant.
MAJOR: AC-4 `ACTIONED` disposition not evidenced: the `!ok || !nr.Enabled` branch still does `delete(p.renewals, store)`, so the renewal bound remains bypassable by toggling a switch; the new `resets` counter merely records it and is never read.

AC-4 observability: new `edp_store_degradation_renewals_total` / `..._resets_total` metrics have no matching rule/alert in this delta (`ops/prometheus` unchanged), so failure-matrix "DEGRADED_EXPIRED -> fail closed + alert" is still alert-less.

Tests: `TestPolicyRenewalLimitFailsClosed` only seeds a pre-filled ledger; no fail-able test covers window pruning/expiry (would have caught the lockout above), the reset path, or that stale entries outside the window are ignored.
MINOR: `main.go` now returns 503 with "store degradation renewal exceeded", leaking operator degradation/renewal state to external callers; keep the body generic and surface detail only in logs/metrics.
`resets map[string]int` is write-only dead state (no reader, no alert); either remove it or expose the count through a metric that is actually alerted.

`RenewalCount` semantics silently changed (cumulative → windowed) and `renewal_limit` / `renewal_window_seconds` were added without runbook/docs updates in this delta, so operator-facing docs drift from behavior.

`degrade` now imports `internal/limits` for counters and exposes an exported mutable `Metrics` field assigned after construction outside the mutex; prefer a constructor/injected sink to avoid coupling and race-prone state.
NIT: `kept := p.renewals[store][:0]` reuses the map value's backing array before `append`, so retained entries alias the stored slice; correct today but opaque and easy to break.

`test_db_explain_capture` asserts the literal `"SELECT"` is absent, but `audit()` is still called with no query/plan, so the redaction path is never exercised and the negative assertion is brittle/vacuous.
SUMMARY: The delta adds configurable renewal window/limit, a distinct error, and counters as claimed, but the window is not enforced on the read path: a store can lock out permanently past the limit.
Reset-on-toggle still defeats the bound (only a dead counter added), and the new renewal/reset metrics are not wired to any alert rule.
Tests pin only the pre-seeded over-limit case, leaving the new windowing and reset logic unverified; overall AC-4 is functional but not safely bounded/observable in production.

BLOCKER: AC-4 `degrade/policy.go` `Check`: the renewal budget is evaluated regardless of whether any switch is active, so after the limit is crossed the (now healthy, switch-cleared/expired) store returns 503 "store unavailable" until entries age out of `renewal_window_seconds` (1h in config) — a self-inflicted outage with no reset path.

Fix must key the bound to an active degradation (and clear/decay the ledger when the switch is cleared/expired), otherwise "bounded, fail-closed degradation" becomes "deny a healthy store for an hour".
MAJOR: `degrade.Load` now hard-requires `renewal_limit>=1`/`renewal_window_seconds>=60` while `version` stays `1` and the schema file is unchanged: any operator-supplied `PF_EDP_DEGRADATION_CONFIG` without the new keys fails `log.Fatalf` at boot (missing migration/defaulting + no version bump).

`reload()` increments the ledger only when `old.Enabled && nr.Enabled && expiry extended`; disable→re-enable (or shorten-then-extend) yields a fresh 900s without consuming the budget, so `RenewalLimit` remains bypassable and total degraded time is unbounded.
`RenewalCount()` returns the raw slice length without window pruning (diverges from `Check`), and the prune logic is duplicated in `reload` and `Check` — two sources of truth for the same invariant.

Observability gap: `ErrRenewalExceeded` denials emit no counter/log and collapse to the same 503 "store unavailable" as a real outage; the alert watches renewals only, so the failure-matrix case `DEGRADED_EXPIRED -> fail closed + alert` is still un-alerted.

MINOR: Prior NIT marked ACTIONED but `kept := p.renewals[store][:0]` aliasing the map value's backing array is still present in `reload()`.

Prior MINOR marked ACTIONED but exported mutable `Policy.Metrics` assigned post-construction remains (nil-checked at two sites); prefer a constructor option/injected sink set before the policy is published.
`reload()` uses wall-clock `time.Now()` while `Check` uses the caller's `now`; no clock injection, so window behaviour is time-dependent in tests and ops replays are not reproducible.

`test_db_explain_capture` still calls `audit()` with no query/plan, so the added `"SELECT" not in text` assertion is vacuous and the redaction path stays untested (ACTIONED disposition does not hold).
`test_edp_degrade_config` only asserts the new keys exist; no fail-able test for missing-key startup failure, window-boundary pruning, or the disable→re-enable counting path.

`store-registry.json`: only the three config files are classified; the AC-1 baseline artifacts and EXPLAIN audit/plan artifacts produced by the new tooling have no retention/backup classification despite the stated retention invariant.
NIT: `len(kept) > p.cfg.RenewalLimit` allows `limit+1` renewals before failing; `renewal_limit: 3` therefore means 3, not "max 3 entries" — document or use `>=`.
`make([]time.Time, 0, len(...))` allocates on every `Check` for every store on the request hot path; prune only when the slice is non-empty/periodically.
`Metrics.Inc` runs under `p.mu` inside `reload`; harmless today but a slow sink would stall all store checks.
Renewal alert is `severity: ticket` with no warning tier before the hard lockout; consider a nearing-limit warning so on-call has lead time.
SUMMARY: Directionally correct fix: per-check window pruning removes the indefinite lockout, the alert and generator are updated together, and the 503 body is now generic.

Remaining risks: the budget is still enforced against a healthy store (availability), the bound is still bypassable via enable/disable transitions, and the customer-facing failure mode is neither labelled per store nor observable as a denial.

Config compatibility was broken silently (new required fields, `version` unchanged, no schema/runbook migration), and the unrelated file-manifest rewrite should be split out and reviewed for secret/artifact leakage.

BLOCKER: none (this delta is metadata-only; it removes no AC evidence and adds no shipped logic). Prior BLOCKERs on `degrade/policy.go` remain unaddressed by this delta and still gate the item.
MAJOR: `store-registry.json`: `ops/prometheus/edp-slo.rules.yml` and `ops/grafana/edp-slo-dashboard.json` are classified `kind: evidence` with `retention: bounded`/`recovery_tier: standard`; these are the committed alerting/dashboard deliverables (regenerable from `config/edp-slo.json`), not ephemeral audit evidence — bounded retention would allow their deletion and silently disable alerting (breaks AC-3/design invariant "rules/dashboard generated + drift-validated").

`gen_docs_index.py`: the new `"Tooling"` category for `EDP-22-RUNBOOK.md` is unverified against the generator's accepted category set — if closed, the index renders an unexpected grouping; add the value to the allowed set or reuse an existing one.

NIT: AC-1 baseline artifacts under `engineering/benchmarks/BI-PF-1314/db/local/` are still unregistered while lower-value files were; register them in the same pass to avoid a fourth follow-up.
SUMMARY: Delta is registry + docs-index metadata only: no AC-1..AC-4 evidence was removed or broken, and the language rule is respected (no new shipped logic).
